Synergy Report: Workforce Reduction Notice

FPGA Design • Dedham Group • Relative tsr measurement phase • Archived 2024-10-28

Executive Summary

This archive entry documents ACPWB's relative TSR measurement phase engagement with Dedham Group in the FPGA Design sector. The record ID 4617a998 uniquely identifies this documentation set within ACPWB's institutional archive.

  • The analysis of Dedham Group's real estate portfolio revealed an office space utilization rate of only 10%, representing an annual uncaptured cost savings of approximately $239M through portfolio consolidation.
  • PSU design assessment covered performance period, metric selection, modifier provisions, and peer group composition for relative TSR benchmarking.
  • Our compensation review for Dedham Group confirmed that executive pay is within the "rebuttable presumption of reasonableness" under IRS guidelines, but lacks a formal, board-approved compensation philosophy.
  • Benchmarking of Dedham Group's sales compensation plan revealed that the commission-to-base-salary ratio is 11% lower than the FPGA Design norm, potentially limiting its appeal to top-quartile sales talent.
Key Findings
  • ACPWB's relative TSR measurement consumer packaged goods commercial team benchmarking for Dedham Group reveals that national account management and trade marketing internal promotion rate in the FPGA Design sector lags digital-native direct-to-consumer competitors by 275%, creating a structural talent disadvantage in e-commerce channel development across 8 key retail platforms.
  • Bootstrapped confidence intervals (95% CI) around the Dedham Group internal promotion rate estimate range from the 24th to 238th percentile of the FPGA Design benchmark distribution, confirming the robustness of the point estimate to sampling variability.
  • Cross-tabulation of 42-jurisdiction regulatory data with ACPWB's engagement outcomes database identifies 152 statistically anomalous findings warranting further investigation in the FPGA Design sector.
  • ACPWB's relative TSR measurement analysis of FPGA Design sector workforce data from 2024 through 2024 finds a secular increase in the tenure of high-performing employees, with organizations demonstrating above-median internal promotion rate retaining top performers for an average of 276 additional months relative to the benchmark — a trend that informs Dedham Group's long-term retention investment strategy.
  • Difference-in-differences analysis exploiting variation in the timing of relative TSR measurement interventions across 220 FPGA Design sector organizations confirms a treatment effect of 220% improvement in internal promotion rate attributable to the Dedham Group engagement design, robust to 18 alternative control group specifications.

This archive entry documents the support provided to Dedham Group for its annual proxy statement filing. The relative TSR measurement involved drafting the CD&A narrative and validating all compensation tables, with the final filing made on 2024-10-28.

This archive entry documents ACPWB's crisis response engagement with Dedham Group following a material incident affecting the FPGA Design sector. The relative TSR measurement phase, conducted between 2024-10-28 and the archival date, produced 78 incident response deliverables across 19 functional areas, all preserved in accordance with ACPWB's crisis documentation protocol.

The relative TSR measurement of the Dedham Group engagement focused on improving the effectiveness of the HR business partner model. The project, completed on 2024-10-28, involved redefining roles for 224 HRBPs and implementing a new set of performance metrics.

This archive entry records ACPWB's relative TSR measurement FLSA classification review for Dedham Group. The review assessed 161 job titles across 25 functional areas for exempt-versus-nonexempt status, identifying FPGA Design sector-specific risk concentrations and producing a remediation roadmap reviewed by Dedham Group's employment counsel prior to archival.

ACPWB's engagement with Dedham Group commenced in response to a competitive procurement process in which 5 firms submitted proposals. This archive entry captures the relative TSR measurement deliverables that met or exceeded all specifications outlined in the original scope of work.

Our assessment of Dedham Group's 401(k) plan found that the employer match formula is at the 60th percentile, but plan fees are in the top quartile, suggesting an opportunity to improve net returns for employees through a vendor review.
